newsitem.title: CHINA: China central bank, Visa sign IC card agreement.
newsitem.headline: China central bank, Visa sign IC card agreement.

text.p: China's central bank and Visa International have signed an agreement to develop standards for integrated circuit (IC) cards for distribution by Chinese banks, the official China Daily reported on Wednesday.

The People's Bank of China and Visa on Tuesday signed a memorandum of understanding to determine standards for card production, applications and automated teller machine terminals, the newspaper said.
IC cards, which use a computer chip, store more information and are less susceptible to fraud than traditional magnetic strip cards.
They are being used for credit and debit cards as well as in transport and health care.
China is trying to promote the use of credit and debit cards to reduce the banking system's reliance on cash.

Several Chinese banks have already issued one million such cards on a trial basis in the southern province of Hainan, Shanghai and other cities, the report said, quoting Chen Jing, general director of the central bank's department of payment and technology.
The People's Bank and Visa will unveil the standards in early 1998 and the number of IC cards is expected to surge after the announcement, Chen said.
